description.text: W. P. Carey Inc. (“W. P. Carey” or the “Company”) is an internally-managed diversified REIT that, together with our consolidated subsidiaries and predecessors, is a leading owner of commercial real estate, net-leased to companies located primarily in the United States and Europe on a long-term basis. The vast majority of our revenues originate from lease revenue provided by our real estate portfolio, which is comprised primarily of single-tenant industrial, warehouse, and retail facilities that are critical to our tenants’ operations. Our portfolio is comprised of 1,682 properties, net-leased to 371 tenants in 25 countries. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 61% of our contractual minimum annualized base rent (“ABR”) was generated by properties located in the United States and approximately 33% was generated by properties located in Europe. As of that same date, our portfolio included 16 operating properties, comprised of 11 self-storage properties, four hotels, and one student housing property. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we sold 63 self-storage operating properties.

Carey organizes its operations into Real Estate and Investment Management segments. The vast majority of the company's income is derived from its Real Estate division in the form of lease revenue from long-term agreements with companies. W.P. Carey's real estate portfolio is primarily comprised of single-tenant office, industrial, warehouse, and retail facilities located around the world. The majority of the company's revenue comes from properties in the U.S. W.P. Carey's Investment Management unit generates revenue from the provision of real estate advisory and portfolio management services to other REITs.

analysis_md:
# WPC — W. P. Carey Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-17. In scope (market cap $14,403,258,023 at $65.14, nasdaq_quote_api). First pass for this name; no prior run in the folder.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
A diversified net-lease REIT (founded 1973): single-tenant, operationally-critical industrial, warehouse and retail properties in the US and Europe under long-term triple-net leases — tenants bear property taxes, insurance and maintenance. As of Q2 2026 (Q2 2026 release, PR Newswire 2026-07-28): 1,748 properties, 188 million sq ft, 384 tenants, weighted-average lease term 12.2 years, occupancy 98.5%, top-10 tenants 18.1% of ABR, ~99% of leases carry escalators (48% CPI-linked, 49% fixed). Q2 2026 AFFO $1.34/share (+4.7% YoY); 2026 AFFO guidance raised and narrowed to $5.19–$5.27/share (+5.2% at midpoint), investment volume assumption raised to $1.7–$2.1B; Q2 investment volume ran at a 7.4% weighted-average initial cash cap rate. Contractual same-store rent growth 2.6% YoY. Dividend $0.95/quarter declared for Q4 2026 ($3.80 annualized, ~73% of FY2025 AFFO). A REIT: the market prices it on AFFO/NAV, not on OCF-minus-capex — see SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH below; this DCF is a cash-discipline check, not the market's model.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $1,716,485,000; net income $466,359,000; operating cash flow $1,282,319,000; capex $135,327,000 — by override, see below (the filer's actual FY2025 line was $191,213,000); SBC $39,894,000 (always a real cost, and small here); D&A $537,645,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $1,107,098,000 = $5.01/share** (financials_history.csv, with the capex override applied).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $868,677,000 — *below* the conservative figure, unusual for a REIT; the gap is non-cash charges (impairments, unrealized losses on the Lineage stake, foreign-debt remeasurement) running through net income. The OCF-based figure is the anchor, as intended.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $8,567,361,000 at FY2025 (engine basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt $8,722,690,000 − cash $155,329,000).
- **OCF quality caveat (material):** GAAP puts proceeds from sales of net investments in sales-type leases inside operating cash flow (ASC 842). Those proceeds were $806,812,000 in FY2024 and $200,168,000 in FY2025 (FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement and MD&A footnote) — asset-sale proceeds, not rent. That is why filed FY2024 OE prints $7.51/share and FY2023 (a spin-off year, below) $4.19/share. The bases are ranked accordingly below.
- Basis break: on November 1, 2023 WPC spun off its office portfolio (NLOP), and in 2025 it sold 63 self-storage operating properties for $784,000,000 of the year's $1,500,000,000 gross dispositions. Pre-2024 revenue/OE history is not the same company; growth inputs below lean on post-break prints and guidance, not the mixed-base 5-yr CAGR.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,282,319,000 − prior YTD $677,196,000 + current YTD $616,370,000 = **TTM $1,221,493,000**
- Capex: **TTM $135,327,000**, all three legs filled by the override, prorated by days (ttm.json overrides_used)
- SBC: FY $39,894,000 − prior YTD $20,091,000 + current YTD $21,350,000 = **TTM $41,153,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **224,609,380**
- **TTM OE total $1,045,013,000 → base OE/share $4.65** (base_source: ttm_json)

## OVERRIDE — capex (filing)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 of the last 3 (dcf_numbers.json data_gap: ["capex"]). WPC files no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment / ProductiveAssets annual fact (the last ProductiveAssets fact in companyfacts is from 2018); its real-estate capital spending appears only as a cash-flow statement line.
- **The decision (bounded authority, kind "filing"):** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 135327000, kind: "filing"}` — the filed FY2024 figure on the line "Funding for real estate construction, redevelopments, and other capital expenditures on real estate", which is also the median of the three filed years ($121,625,000 FY2023 / $135,327,000 FY2024 / $191,213,000 FY2025), from the FY2025 10-K Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0001025378-26-000036). The engine applies the single value to every missing period (2016–2025 in the history). Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2023 capex by $13,702,000 (~1.3% of FY2023 OCF, lowering that year's OE — conservative direction), is exact for FY2024, and understates FY2025 capex by $55,886,000, flattering FY2025 OE by ~$0.25/share; FY2025 feeds the normalized median but is *not* the base used (the TTM pin is), so the flattered year does not set the verdict. - **OVERRIDE_OUT_OF_BAND:capex:** mechanical only — the band is computed against the last filed value under an engine-read tag and there is no filed value at all; judgment.json carries an ack_reason stating exactly that. This is a filing-sourced figure, not an unanchored estimate.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: Durable contractual cash flows (12.2y WALT, escalators on ~99% of leases, 98.5% occupancy, 384 tenants) plus an investment-grade cost-of-capital and sourcing advantage — but net lease is commodity capital with no pricing power past market cap rates, thin cap-rate-over-funding spreads, and growth bought with dilutive external capital.
- FOR: contractual duration — 12.2-year weighted-average lease term, 98.5% occupancy, ~99% of leases with escalators (48% CPI-linked, 49% fixed), 2.6% contractual same-store rent growth; diversification — 1,748 properties, 384 tenants, top-10 only 18.1% of ABR, US + Europe; cost-of-capital advantage — BBB+/Baa1 investment-grade unsecured access, 3.2% weighted-average debt rate and $2.7B liquidity at Q2 2026, forward-equity ATM machine; sale-leaseback sourcing franchise built since 1973.
- AGAINST: no pricing power beyond market cap rates at origination/renewal — net lease is commodity capital; growth is externally funded (share count +3.3%/yr) so per-share compounding leaks to new shareholders; returns are the cap-rate/funding-cost spread, which a higher-for-longer regime compresses; tenant credit events recur (Hellweg insolvency in 2026 — exposure cut to ~0.9% of ABR per the Q2 call; Q2 2026 impairments $79,400,000) and single-tenant assets are binary on default; ~73% AFFO payout retains little.
- ROIC evidence, as required: fundamentals.json produces **no roic_proxy series for WPC** (no operating-income series in its extraction) and its ~99% "gross margin" is a rental-accounting artifact (rent as revenue, property costs borne by tenants and recorded below the line), so neither series can carry the score. The 5/10 rests on the contractual/structural evidence above and sits in line with scored peers (KIM 5, EXR 5, CCI 6, VICI 7 — VICI's scarcer experiential assets and CCI's tower scarcity both rate above a diversified commodity net-lease book).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Method range: the defensible bases span the normalized median $5.01/share (FY2025, still carrying $200M of asset-sale proceeds in OCF) down to the TTM $4.65 used, and ~$4.50 ex-proceeds. Every one of them lands Tier C at $65.14 — the tier is robust to the base choice even though the point IRR is not (11.15% weighted on the TTM pin vs 12.88% on the zero-fill native run).
- What the model is really saying: at $65.14 you are paying ~14.0x TTM OE and ~12.5x guided AFFO for contractual ~2.6% internal growth plus whatever spread external growth adds. That prices in competent execution forever. The 15% hurdle needs $44.43 — a ~32% drawdown, or years of retained compounding at a flat price.
- Watch items: Hellweg resolution (springing leases on half the remaining stores per the Q2 call), Q2 2026 impairments of $79,400,000 as a tenant-credit tell, the pace of forward-equity settlement (dilution timing), and whether the 7.4% going-in cap rate holds as the $1.7–$2.1B program deploys.
- Enrichment note: all step-9 enrichments ran clean after scoring — fundamentals, prices, segments, statements, profile/street and reprice all wrote their files; no failures to note.
